name: Univariate Theil–Sen regression
definition: For distinct predictor pairs, set β̂=median_((i,j):i<j,x_i≠x_j)[(y_j−y_i)/(x_j−x_i)] and α̂=median_i(y_i−β̂x_i). Predict ŷ=α̂+β̂x.
variables: x continuous predictor, y response, α̂ joint-median intercept, β̂ slope
assumptions: At least two distinct x values and a meaningful single linear trend
limitations: Quadratic pair enumeration and weak identification when predictors are tightly clustered
failure_conditions: Quadratic pair enumeration and weak identification when predictors are tightly clustered
computation: O(n²) pair slopes and storage before median selection

name: Siegel repeated-median regression
definition: For each i with an available nonvertical pair, set b_i=median_(j:x_j≠x_i)[(y_j−y_i)/(x_j−x_i)]. Then β̂=median_i b_i and α̂=median_i(y_i−β̂x_i).
variables: x continuous predictor, y response, b_i local slope median, α̂ joint residual median
assumptions: At least two distinct predictor values; robust simple linear trend is the target
limitations: Can be expensive for large tables, and duplicate predictor values reduce usable slopes
failure_conditions: Can be expensive for large tables, and duplicate predictor values reduce usable slopes
computation: O(n²) pair computations before median operations

name: RANSAC consensus regression
definition: For T trials draw a small subset S, fit θ_S, then let I_S={i: ℓ(y_i,f(x_i;θ_S))≤τ}. Select the candidate with maximum |I_S|, break ties by the declared inlier fit criterion, and refit the model on its inliers.
variables: x,y regression data, θ parameters, ℓ point loss, τ threshold, T trial budget, I_S inlier set
assumptions: At least one nondegenerate all-inlier subset can be sampled with meaningful probability
limitations: Poor threshold or competing regimes can select a majority relation unrelated to the target
failure_conditions: Poor threshold or competing regimes can select a majority relation unrelated to the target
computation: T small fits and O(Tn) residual evaluations, followed by one inlier refit

source.citation: Scikit-learn maintainers’ linear models guide, RANSAC. https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html#ransac-random-sample-consensus

name: Raw minimum covariance determinant estimator
definition: For a declared h, find H*=argmin_(H⊆{1,…,n}, |H|=h) det S_H, where S_H=h⁻¹Σ_(i∈H)(x_i−μ_H)(x_i−μ_H)ᵀ and μ_H=h⁻¹Σ_(i∈H)x_i. Return (μ_H*,S_H*) before consistency correction or reweighting.
variables: x_i∈ℝ^d, n sample count, h support count, μ_H subset mean, S_H subset covariance
assumptions: d+1≤h≤n and data in general position for nonsingular support subsets
limitations: Near-singular clouds make determinant comparisons unstable, and a single robust ellipsoid poorly represents multiple clusters
failure_conditions: Near-singular clouds make determinant comparisons unstable, and a single robust ellipsoid poorly represents multiple clusters
computation: Exact subset search examines binomial(n,h) supports; practical approximate solvers use concentration steps

source.citation: Scikit-learn maintainers’ covariance guide, Minimum Covariance Determinant. https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/covariance.html#minimum-covariance-determinant
